answer: Hardware-rooted identity attestation stops Sybils in four steps. First, each agent registers a TPM endorsement key proving distinct physical hardware. Second, the server sends a nonce the chip must sign, so one machine cannot pose as many. Third, duplicate keys are rejected at the door, and a whisper of fraud freezes the batch. Fourth, monthly re-attestation catches any agent that goes quiet. Faking 1,000 agents needs 1,000 real chips at $40 each, about $40,000 in hardware, lost if caught. Each voyage starts at one vertex, like a market where every stall needs its own license plate.
